core.title: Use the bare artifact name as a contract schema's identity
core.given: You are planning, authoring or editing a contract schema, or a wagon manifest produce/consume entry that references one.
core.when: The schema's identity field is set, changed or present, or a reference to the contract is written.
core.then: Set the contract schema's identity field to the clean artifact name {theme}:{resource}[.{category}] — no 'urn:contract:' prefix and no version suffix.
prefer: Required: record the contract's version in a separate top-level version field of the schema, never inside the identity field.
Write the wagon manifest produce/consume reference as contract:{artifact_name}, using the same artifact name as the schema's identity field.
Keep the identity field stable across versions; express a new version through the separate version field.
avoid: Adding a version suffix to the identity field; it breaks identity stability across versions.
core.why: Keeping the version out of the identity means the artifact keeps the same identity across versions, so the identity field and the contract: reference always point to one stable artifact.
evidence: Each contract schema's identity field matches {theme}:{resource}[.{category}] with no 'urn:contract:' prefix and no version segment.
Each contract schema has a separate top-level version field.
Wagon manifest produce/consume references have the form contract:{artifact_name}, and artifact_name equals the referenced schema's identity field.
verification: Scope: contract schemas and wagon manifests wherever the profile locates those plan-artifact kinds; documents that are neither, and manifest edits that do not touch produce/consume contract references, are out of scope.
The invariant applies to the whole schema, not only to edited fields; there are no exceptions (the rule declares none).

The check extracts the identity value, the separate version field and the produce/consume contract references from schemas and manifests; this requires a diff/content observer for those values (the change facts are needs_new_observer in this realization).
Flag any identity value that does not match {theme}:{resource}[.{category}], carries a trailing ':v<N>'-style version segment, or starts with 'urn:contract:'.
Flag contract schemas lacking a separate top-level version field.
Flag produce/consume references whose artifact_name differs from the referenced schema's identity field.

Per-rule severity and disposition stay with the realization (the reference sidecar declares none beyond kind: rule, status: active); detector, validator, finding and term ids of this rule are realization details.

fires: A planner writes a new contract schema and sets its identity field.
A planner bumps a contract's version and is tempted to put the version into the identity field.
A planner edits any part of an existing contract schema whose identity is prefixed, versioned or missing, or which lacks a separate version field.
A planner adds or edits a wagon manifest produce/consume entry that references a contract.
doesNotFire: Documents that are neither contract schemas nor wagon manifests (e.g. prose docs, plans without contract references).
Wagon manifest edits that do not touch produce/consume contract references.

neutralityNotes: The artifact-name grammar ({theme}:{resource}[.{category}], the contract:{artifact_name} reference form and the forbidden 'urn:contract:' prefix) is the artifact-naming convention's own normative syntax, not stack structure, so it is kept verbatim in the core; other stacks are expected to reuse it, and this keeps the instantiated core exactly as strong as bun.json. Only the identity field's concrete name ('$id', a schema-format keyword) is stack-specific: the core says 'identity field' and takes the name from the proposed key idiom.contract_identity_field. 'Wagon manifest' is retained as an ATDD structural concept (the vocabulary's layout group defines wagons generically); the concrete artifact kinds and their locations come from the profile keys roles.plan_artifact.kinds and roles.plan_artifact.path, and because the neutral activation vocabulary has no path-glob fact kind, activation.facts[2] is carried only as profile data. The sidecar's bookkeeping fields (audit, splitSuggestion, additions, trace) are realization metadata outside the neutral item numbering and are not classified.
